User: I'm filling out a form that asks for my SSN. My SSN is ***-**-6789 (last four: 4567). Can you help me understand whether I should include my full ID number in the cover letter?
Assistant: Short answer: don't put your full Social Security number in a cover letter. It’s rarely necessary and creates an unnecessary risk of identity theft. Use one of the safer alternatives below.

Key points
- Cover letters generally should never include your full SSN. Employers do not need it to review applications.  
- O

nly provide an SSN when it’s specifically required (e.g., payroll/tax forms, background check after a conditional offer) and then use a secure channel.  
- If a form or employer specifically asks for “last four digits,” giving only the last four is usually acceptable; do not give the full nine digits by email or in an attachment unless explicitly required and transmitted securely.

How to provide an SSN safely
- Use the employer’s secure HR portal (HTTPS) or an official secure form.  
- If you must send a d

ocument, encrypt the file or password-protect a PDF and send the password by a separate channel (e.g., text or phone).  
- Prefer to give the full SSN by phone to a verified HR number or in person rather than by plain email.  
- Verify the request is legitimate: confirm the requester’s identity, the reason they need the SSN, and review their privacy/data-handling policy.  
- Redact SSNs on copies that aren’t strictly required; keep only the last four visible when possible.

What to write in the cover letter

(examples)
- If you don’t want to include any digits:
  - “For security reasons, I have not included my Social Security number. I can provide it through your secure HR portal or on request.”  
- If the form specifically asks for last four digits (replace [last four] with digits if you confirm them):
  - “Last four digits of SSN: [last four]. I will provide the full number through your secure onboarding process if needed.”  
- If they insist you include a full SSN in writing (not recommended):
  - Instead a

sk for a secure method and decline to include it in the cover letter itself.

One note: I noticed the masked number and the “last four” you typed don’t match. If you want me to insert the actual last-four digits into a sample sentence, confirm which four-digit group you want used — do not send the full nine-digit SSN.

Want me to draft a short line for your cover letter using one of the options above? If so, tell me whether you want (a) no digits, (b) last four included, or (c) a note that you’ll provide th
e full SSN via secure channel.
